Approach and rationale
The existing methods rely on continuous optimization and simulated annealing for binary solutions, which can struggle with escaping local optima like the current best solution around 0.3809. My strategy shifts to a structured optimization of axis-aligned rectangles, assuming the optimal solution has a sparse representation. Instead of searching all possible configurations, I parameterize the solution by selecting and positioning three rectangles (each defined by two corners). The objective is computed by aggregating non-overlapping rectangle contributions, enabling efficient calculation of the correlation integral. Bayesian optimization then tunes these rectangles to minimize the maximum overlap, leveraging automatic derivative calculation from the parameterized form.

The key novelty is treating the step function as a combination of axis-aligned rectangles and using their positional parameters directly as optimization variables.
